cover_letter.greeting: Dear Con Edison Enterprise Risk Management Team,
paragraphs: I'm applying for the Project Specialist, Finance role on Con Edison's Enterprise Risk Management team. I'm an MBA Finance (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli, and before that I worked at JPMorgan Asset Management, Lenovo and Thomson Reuters. Energy is the sector I most want to work in, and an ERM seat that touches every part of Con Edison's operations, with work that goes to the Board and the Department of Public Service, is a rare way to learn how a utility actually runs.

Much of my work has been turning numbers into material for senior people. At JPMorgan Asset Management I prepared executive-level briefs on capital allocation for senior leadership and benchmarked past marketing-channel budget allocations, which found 30% in efficiency gains. At Lenovo I ran variance and sensitivity analyses on budget changes, built forecasts and scenario analyses that improved capital efficiency by 15%, and turned the findings into recommendations for teams across the business.

That maps to compiling risk metrics, building department risk portfolios and preparing ERM presentations. I haven't worked in formal enterprise risk management before, so I'd start by learning your framework and the businesses the risk leaders run. I stay organized across many deadlines, I'm comfortable working with senior stakeholders, and I'm careful with the numbers that end up in front of a committee. I'd welcome the chance to talk.
